headline: High-risk shared-workspace and command-execution overlap: prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors are plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write workspace files, so content produced by one can be consumed by the other through the shared filesystem. Replit Agent’s per-Repl persistent filesystem and Windsurf’s local filesystem sharing create a plausible injection bridge even without MCP. This is not merely manual copy-paste because file content can be treated as trusted input.
conditions: IF either agent reads instructions from files written by the other without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace directory, attacker-controlled file content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of file contents as instructions.
Add provenance labels to inter-agent files.
Require manual review before executing file-derived commands.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code, and agent_a also touches secrets while agent_b has broad network egress and can use MCP servers. A shared workspace or copied files can move sensitive material from Replit Agent into Windsurf’s context, where it may be transmitted onward. The exact leakage path is not fully documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment configuration from agent_a are placed in shared files, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b forwards workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP servers, sensitive data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files.
Review outbound network destinations before running either agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification. Agent_a persists across Repl sessions, while agent_b shares state via local filesystem, so concurrent edits can collide without a documented lock. That overlap can corrupt code or git history, and the rubric treats same-dir unrestricted writes plus git modification as high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, conflicting writes can overwrite each other.
IF either agent auto-commits or rewrites branches while the other is active, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Run git status before and after each handoff.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b can treat files or outputs from agent_a as input, and both agents can act on shell and git commands. If Replit Agent’s output is accepted without verification, Windsurf may propagate mistakes into edits or commands. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, but the pathway is not guaranteed to be fully automatic, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated plans or code without review, errors can cascade into edits or commits.
IF agent_a emits incorrect commands that agent_b reuses, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Limit one agent to drafting only.
Compare outputs against source files before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent_a explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration, while agent_b handles open files and can use broad network egress plus MCP. If regulated or sensitive data is moved from Replit Agent into Windsurf, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR certifications, so the safest supported finding is a medium compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in shared workspace files, both agents may process it under different retention/logging regimes.
IF secrets or customer data are copied from agent_a into agent_b sessions, compliance obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
